Studios

🎨 Overlay Studio

Design poster overlays (ratings, resolution, awards…) in a visual editor and apply them to your whole library — filtered targeting, nightly re-apply, clean-art restore.

🗂️ Collection Studio

Build living collections — charts, franchises, universes, seasonal windows, smart rules — with generated posters, server sync, and wishlist tie-ins.

Database & Scanning

💾 Backups

Verified snapshots of the video database (wishlist, watchlist, history, settings). The nightly automation keeps a rolling set; restore stages a swap for the next restart — your current database is set aside, never deleted.

⏳ A restore is staged — it applies on the next restart.

✏️ Mass Rename

Re-render every file name to your current naming templates (Settings → Organization). Preview first — nothing moves until you apply. Subtitles and sidecars travel with their file; the server re-adopts the names on its next scan.

Connections Accounts, media servers, and API keys SYNCHRO.S connects to

Metadata Source

i
Where artist, album, and track metadata comes from:
• Spotify — official Spotify; connect your account with the Spotify tile under Services.
• Spotify (no auth) — the same Spotify catalog with no account needed. It's unofficial and best-effort (may break if Spotify changes its site) and can't read your personal library or playlists.
• Deezer / iTunes — free, no account.
• MusicBrainz — free; the public server is limited to 1 request/sec. Configure a self-hosted server in the MusicBrainz tile under Services.
• Discogs — needs a personal access token.
• JioSaavn — opt in under Advanced → Experimental. Strong for Indian and Bollywood catalogs.

Tip: if you pick Spotify (no auth) and later connect a real Spotify account, it uses the official account normally and only falls back to no-auth while Spotify is rate-limited — then switches back automatically.
Services Accounts and API keys SYNCHRO.S connects to

TMDB & TVDB are required. The video side matches, enriches and automates everything from these — library matching, artwork, airing shows, collections — so nothing works until both keys are set. Both are free. OMDb and fanart.tv below are optional extras.

Service

API Configuration

Spotify

›
Current Redirect URI:
http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback
Add this URL to your Spotify app's 'Redirect URIs' in the Spotify Developer Dashboard. Spotify requires HTTPS for any URI that isn't loopback — on a NAS or remote server, enter an HTTPS proxy URL in the Redirect URI field above instead (see Help & Docs → Getting Started).
i
Runs the background metadata enrichment worker on the no-auth Spotify source instead of this connected account — keeping bulk enrichment off your official API quota (and dodging rate-limit bans), so your account is reserved for interactive search and playlist sync. On by default. Turn off to enrich through your connected account instead. Works even with no account connected. Note: the no-auth source can't supply artist genres.

iTunes / Apple Music

›
Sets the primary Apple Music storefront. Region-specific albums are auto-searched across other storefronts as fallback.

Deezer (Favorites & Playlists)

›
Current Redirect URI:
http://127.0.0.1:8008/deezer/callback
Add this URL to your Deezer app at developers.deezer.com
Or use an ARL token for playlist access and downloads (no OAuth app needed):
Log into deezer.com → DevTools (F12) → Application → Cookies → copy the arl value. Provides playlist access + downloads.

Discogs

›
Get your free token from Discogs Developer Settings
Click "Generate new token" — no app registration needed. Provides 60 req/min and cover art in search results.

Tidal (Playlists & Metadata)

›
Current Redirect URI:
http://127.0.0.1:8889/tidal/callback
Add this URL to your Tidal app configuration

Qobuz (Metadata & Enrichment)

›
Connects Qobuz for metadata enrichment (ISRC, labels, copyright). Also used for downloads if Qobuz is your download source.
Alternative: Auth Token — If email/password login fails (CAPTCHA), paste your token directly:
To get your token: log into play.qobuz.com → DevTools (F12) → Network tab → find any request to www.qobuz.com/api.json → look in the request headers for X-User-Auth-Token → copy that value.

Concerts

›
Adds a Live section to artist pages. Both are optional and independent — set up either, both, or neither.
Upcoming dates, venues and ticket links. Free self-service key from developer.ticketmaster.com (5,000 calls a day).
Two letters, like US or GB. Keeps the concerts in your Discover inbox to one country. Leave it empty for everywhere. Artist pages always show every date.
What the artist actually played at recent shows, song by song — and a setlist can be played straight from your library. Free key from setlist.fm/settings/api (non-commercial use).

Last.fm

›
The Last.fm account whose listening history to import. You can correct this username here or on the Stats page.
Get your API key and secret from Last.fm API Account
API key: used for metadata enrichment. API secret: required for scrobbling.

Genius

›
Get your token from Genius API Clients
Generate a "Client Access Token" — no OAuth flow needed.

MusicBrainz

›
Optional: enter your self-hosted server address. Leave blank to use public MusicBrainz. Applies to search, matching and enrichment as soon as settings are saved.
For a fixed limit, enter requests/second (for example, 10). With No limit (adaptive), SYNCHRO.S will try to find the maximum number of requests/second your server can handle. Only use this when you host the MusicBrainz server yourself and it has no other traffic. Public MusicBrainz always keeps its rate limit. Environment overrides take precedence over these fields. Your server needs search indexes; use its final URL.

AcoustID Verification

›
Verifies downloaded audio matches expected track using fingerprints
Requires an Application API key (not your user account key) — register a free application at acoustid.org/new-application
The fpcalc fingerprint tool is automatically downloaded if needed. Failed verifications move files to Quarantine folder.

ListenBrainz

›
Get your token from ListenBrainz Settings
Self-hosted? Enter your server URL (e.g. http://localhost:8093)
Maloja: use http://your-server:42010/apis/listenbrainz and your Maloja API key. Start history sync from Stats.

Hydrabase

›
P2P metadata network. When enabled and connected, replaces Spotify/iTunes as the primary metadata source for searches.

Free community APIs — no key needed. Gap-fill extra data on your library in the background.

Free community APIs — no key needed. Enrich cached YouTube videos in the background.

Video Quality

Ladder, cutoff, rejects & tie-breakers
Profiles apply per title: everything uses Default unless you assign another profile from a movie/show's Manage panel. Quality is read from the release name — pick the ladder you'll accept, where to stop upgrading, what to reject outright, then the soft tie-breakers.
Quality ladder toggle what you'll accept · rank best→worst with the arrows
Upgrade until once you have this resolution (or better) stop chasing upgrades
Never grab hard rejects — skipped no matter what else matches
Preferences soft tie-breakers — they rank candidates, they never reject on their own
Codec
HDR
Audio
Max size skip anything bigger — set per type so a movie and an episode aren't judged the same
Movie No limit
TV episode No limit
Minimum seeders At least 1 seeder
A torrent nobody is seeding never finishes — it parks on "downloading metadata" or stalls at 0% and quietly fills your client with dead entries. Set 0 to grab regardless. Usenet and Soulseek have no seeders and are never affected.

Custom Formats

Score releases by their name — prefer trusted groups, bury x265, chase freeleech, anything a pattern can see. Terms are plain substrings, or regex written /x265|hevc/. A format matches when all "match" terms hit and no "never" term does; matching formats add their score to a release's rank (negative buries without rejecting). The "this profile" column overrides a format's score for the profile selected above.
Releases whose summed format score falls below this are rejected outright. 0 = off.

Source, stream & concurrency
i
Choose where to download music from. Hybrid mode tries primary source first, then falls back to secondary if it fails.
Available drag one across, or click it
Download chain

Download Sources

Set up any source here, then put it in the chain on the Downloads tab. A source does not have to be enabled to be configured.
💡 Filesystem access — easiest setup ▾
Torrent and usenet clients write files to their own download folders, not Soulseek's. SYNCHRO.S needs read access to those folders to import the files. Simplest fix: point all your downloaders (Soulseek, qBittorrent, SABnzbd / NZBGet) at the same download folder. One folder, one path to worry about, everything just works.
  • Bare-metal: just set every client's download path to the same folder (e.g. your existing slskd folder). Done.
  • Docker: easiest is to reuse the ./downloads mount you already have for slskd — point qBit and SAB at /downloads inside their containers too. Or use the commented placeholders in docker-compose.yml if you want separate folders.
  • Remote client (NAS / different host): mount the remote folder locally (SMB / NFS / rclone) before SYNCHRO.S can see it.
Keeps what you share on Soulseek up to date with your library. The network blocks people who share nothing.
How long to search for tracks (15-300 seconds)
Extra time to wait for late results (5-60 seconds)
Forces a gap between consecutive searches. Smooths burst patterns that trip ISP anti-abuse (e.g. Bell Canada cuts the WAN after rapid peer-connection spikes). 0 disables.
Ignore search results from peers with upload speed below this threshold
Skip peers with a queue longer than this (prefers peers with shorter queues regardless)
Off by default. Applies to automatic tracks and album bundles when another eligible peer is available; not manually chosen files.
When enabled, try the next Soulseek candidate after roughly one minute below this observed speed. Uses actual byte progress rather than the peer's advertised speed. The final available candidate is always allowed to continue. 0 also disables.
Abandon stuck downloads after this many minutes
Automatically cleans old searches from slskd when over 200 entries. Disable if you want to keep manual searches in slskd's queue.
Which transfers and searches cleanup removes. Leave on "own" if other apps (Lidarr, another SYNCHRO.S, slskd's own UI) share this slskd. "Everything" clears all clients' finished downloads and is only safe when SYNCHRO.S is the only user.
Requires a paid Qobuz subscription. Streams are DRM-free.
Alternative: Auth Token — If email/password login fails (CAPTCHA), paste your token directly:
To get your token: log into play.qobuz.com → DevTools (F12) → Network tab → find any request to www.qobuz.com/api.json → look for X-User-Auth-Token in the request headers → copy that value.
Free lossless downloads via community-run hifi-api instances. No authentication or subscription needed.
Heads up: some HiFi instances only have 30-second Tidal previews for certain tracks, with headers faked to look like the full song. SYNCHRO.S decodes every HiFi download to catch these and never lets a shorter clip replace a good library file, but if a track just won't come through at full length here, grab it from another source.
Your ARL token authenticates with Deezer. To get it: log into deezer.com → open browser DevTools (F12) → Application tab → Cookies → copy the arl value.
SoundCloud downloads run anonymously — no account required. Use this for DJ mixes, remixes, and tracks that aren't on Spotify/Tidal/Deezer.

Quality: 128 kbps MP3 / AAC depending on the upload (anonymous tier). SoundCloud doesn't expose lossless audio to anyone.
Full URL to your Lidarr instance (e.g. http://192.168.1.100:8686)
Found in Lidarr → Settings → General → Security → API Key
Uses Lidarr's indexers and download clients (Usenet/torrent) for album downloads.

Best for full-album grabs. Lidarr is album-first by design — track-name searches usually return nothing useful, so in hybrid mode Lidarr is mostly a no-op for playlists and falls through to your other sources. Use Lidarr Only when you specifically want to grab whole albums via your indexers.
Only needed for private playlists, your Liked Music, age-gated videos and Premium audio qualities — public videos download fine with None. Reading a browser only works when that browser is on the same machine as SYNCHRO.S, so on a server or in Docker choose Paste cookies.txt. On Windows, Chrome and the other Chromium browsers seal their cookies in a way yt-dlp cannot read at all — use Firefox or Paste cookies.txt.
For server/Docker installs with no local browser. Paste a Netscape/Mozilla cookies.txt. Export with a "Get cookies.txt LOCALLY" extension and paste the whole file — the # Netscape HTTP Cookie File header alone is not enough. Required for private playlists like your Liked Music, and for Premium audio itags. Cookies expire periodically — re-paste if YouTube stops working.
Seconds between YouTube downloads to avoid bot detection. Default: 3
i
YouTube serves Opus or AAC, not FLAC or MP3. With this on, the quality list must include the converted format (default MP3 320). With it off, add Opus or AAC to the list, or turn Fallback on.

yt-dlp ●

i
YouTube changes how it serves video far more often than yt-dlp cuts a stable release, so nightly is what actually keeps downloads working. Stable is there if you'd rather move slowly.
When YouTube downloads start failing with 403 Forbidden, an out-of-date yt-dlp is nearly always the cause. An update only takes effect after you restart SYNCHRO.S — the running process keeps using the version it loaded at startup.
